actual_scope: The different-mask one-new-pair exchange for the six-source weight-3 count at characteristic 7, under the inherited centre-only free-type hypothesis. The question is the weight-3 cover when (10, 14) and (11, 13) share different masks and exactly one of those sums is weight 3. This package shows the weight-3 end is a (10, 14) shape, that there are 2160 such routes, and that the cover is 3, or 4 on the complement endpoints. Unrestricted c=7 existence stays open.
scope_change_reason: The catalogue card asks for one new connector operation. This package keeps the unsigned dirty connector alphabet fixed and answers open question 1 of PR #7045: the shared-mask walks on which exactly one of (10, 14) and (11, 13) is weight 3 and the two masks differ. A new operation is not the missing step.
bottleneck_link: Side result on the recursive-interface schedule. It does not change a supplier, a consumer, or kappa. It computes the weight-3 cover of the different-mask one-new-pair walks at c=7 and leaves the same-mask half, other weights, and the full depth-two question open.
stop_rule: Stop once every centre-only different-mask chain with exactly one of (10, 14) and (11, 13) weight 3 has its weight-3 cover classified, or stop if one such chain has cover 20.
evidence: Exhaustive free-type census. The (11, 13) shapes cannot change mask, so the weight-3 end is one of the 180 (10, 14) shapes. Each shape has four different masks at (11, 13) and three routes through s=12, 2160 routes in all. The diagonal image together with R is {M, N, R}. (9, 15) adds M^c only for the complement endpoints. The cover is 3 or 4, both attained by explicit words. No supplier, consumer, or selected conditional kappa changes. The selected record remains 363005817/100000000000.

open_questions.question: On a centre-only chain where s=10 and s=14 share a mask, s=11 and s=13 share that same mask, and exactly one of the two sums is weight 3, what is the weight-3 cover?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The different-mask half is settled at cover 3 or 4. The same-mask half is the remaining one-new-pair subfamily of the shared-mask walks counted by PR #7045, which classified only the subcase in which both sums are weight 3.
